svg.aria-label: Animated comparison of one thread's work per k step. Before, it loads 8 values of A and 8 of B from shared memory and does 64 multiply-adds into an 8 by 8 patch of C; the block tile is 128 by 128 with 256 threads. After, the patch is 16 by 8: 16 values of A and 8 of B, 24 loads, feed 128 multiply-adds, and the block tile is 128 by 256, still 256 threads. Bars compare 16 over 64 with 24 over 128: the bigger patch needs fewer shared-memory loads per multiply-add. Below, one SM's register file drawn to scale: before, two blocks of 256 threads at 128 registers each fill it; after, 237 registers per thread make one block take nearly all of it, leaving no room for a second block, so one block runs per SM.
svg.text: loads from shared memory feed multiply-adds into registers

text.class: b sm on-blk a w5 fin
b sm on-blk a w5 fin
b sm on-blk a w6 fin

svg.text: Before: 8 values of A and 8 of B per k step.
Every A–B pair updates one entry of the patch.
After: twice the rows means 16 values of A, but still only 8 of B.
Twice the multiply-adds for 1.5× the loads (24 vs 16).
The same 8 B values now serve twice as many rows.
Before: one block's loads could overlap the other's math.
Each thread's 128 running sums must stay in registers.
A bigger patch trades registers for fewer shared-memory loads per multiply-add.
